record.paper_title: Some open questions in axion theory
record.original_question: How is the axion potential generated by magnetic monopoles modified in a thermal bath of relativistic charged particles, where plasma screening changes the long-distance electric fields and therefore changes the monopole-induced axion potential relevant for cosmological applications?

evidence.quote: Therefore, it is important to determine how the monopole-generated axion potential gets modified in the presence of a bath of relativistic charged particles which would cause screening of electric fields at large distances.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a U(1) gauge theory containing magnetic monopoles of mass $M$ and magnetic charge $g = 2\pi/e$ coupled to a pseudoscalar axion field $a$ with decay constant $f_a$ through the topological term $\mathcal{L} \supset (a/f_a)(e^2/8\pi^2) F_{\mu\nu}\tilde F^{\mu\nu}$. Via the Witten effect, in the vacuum a monopole acquires an electric charge $q(a) = e\,a/(2\pi f_a)$, and integrating out (or summing over) monopole loops produces a periodic axion potential $V_0(a)$ whose form is determined by the long-range Coulomb electric field sourced by the dyonic charge.

Now place this system in a thermal bath at temperature $T$ of relativistic charged particles of charge $e$ and number density appropriate to thermal equilibrium, so that the photon develops a Debye screening mass $m_D(T) \sim eT$ and the electric field of a dyon is screened beyond distances of order $m_D^{-1}$ rather than falling off as $1/r^2$.

Determine the monopole-induced effective axion potential $V(a;T)$ in this screened plasma, including its dependence on $T$, $m_D(T)$, $M$, $e$, and $f_a$. In particular, derive how plasma screening modifies the contribution of a single monopole (or monopole–antimonopole configuration) to $V(a;T)$ compared with the vacuum result $V_0(a)$, and identify the parametric regime (relating $T$, $M$, and $m_D$) in which the screened potential is relevant for cosmology.
artifact.status_search_result: No publication appears to give a complete derivation of the monopole-induced axion potential in a screened relativistic plasma. The vacuum monopole-loop computation of the axion potential is established, and plasma screening of dyon electric fields is well-known qualitatively, but the explicit finite-temperature modification of the monopole-generated axion potential relevant for cosmology remains an open computational problem.

status_evidence.title: Axion Mass from Magnetic Monopole Loops
status_evidence.snippet: Axions interacting with Abelian gauge fields obtain a potential from loops of magnetic monopoles as a consequence of the Witten effect.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the vacuum monopole-generated axion potential, the starting point that needs to be modified by plasma screening.

status_evidence.title: Experimental Observation of Space-Charge Field Screening of a Relativistic Particle Bunch in Plasma
status_evidence.snippet: Plasma screens the space-charge field when distances are much larger than the plasma skin depth.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the physical mechanism (Debye/plasma screening of long-range electric fields) entering the proposed modification, but does not provide the axion potential result.
